featured_reviews.name: Burjiz
featured_reviews.review_text:
Golden Chimney offered a comfortable and enjoyable dining experience during our visit.

The ambience inside the restaurant was quite good, especially after entering from the outside summer heat into the air-conditioned seating area.

There happened to be an IPL match playing during the visit as well, which added a lively atmosphere without making the place feel too noisy or chaotic.

For drinks, I ordered a fresh lime water, which was refreshing and suited the weather well.

For starters, we ordered the Murgh Lasoni Tikka and Classic Chicken Chilly. Both dishes were enjoyable, though the Murgh Lasoni Tikka stood out more for its flavour and preparation.

For the mains, we had the Butter Chicken, which was well prepared and satisfying.

Service was good, seating was comfortable, and overall the restaurant provided a pleasant dine-in experience.

All in all, a good restaurant option in the Opera House / Lamington Road area for a relaxed lunch or dinner with decent food and ambience.

featured_reviews.name: Anmol Sanyasi
featured_reviews.review_text:
From the very first meal, Golden Chimney completely won us over. The food is absolutely delicious — every dish is rich in flavor, beautifully balanced, and full of authentic taste. You can truly taste Mumbai in the food — the spices, the freshness, and the variety all come together perfectly. Each bite felt thoughtfully prepared and full of character.
What made our experience even more special was the staff. They are incredibly gentle, kind, and genuinely thoughtful. The hospitality here stands out. They pay attention to every detail and make sure you feel comfortable and taken care of. Whether it was helping us choose dishes or checking in to make sure everything was perfect, their service was warm and sincere. We were visiting Mumbai from outside the city for just four days, and we ended up eating at Golden Chimney four out of five days — that says everything. When you find a place that combines amazing food with outstanding hospitality, you naturally want to return. Every time we came back, the quality was consistent and impressive.
The money we spent was absolutely worth it.
The portion sizes, the flavor, the cleanliness, and the service all reflect great value for the price.
It's rare to find a restaurant where both the food and the people leave such a lasting impression.
If you're in Mumbai and want authentic, flavorful food with heartfelt hospitality, Golden Chimney is a must-visit. We will definitely return the next time we are in the city.

featured_reviews.name: Burjiz
featured_reviews.review_text:
Flute 24 Hrs had a mixed dining experience overall.

The starters were quite good and flavourful. We ordered the Korean Style Chicken and Murgh Phoolzadi Kebab, both of which were enjoyable and well prepared.

However, the mains was a disappointment. We ordered the Murg Angara, and it lacked proper flavour and tasted quite off compared to the strong start from the appetizers. I also felt the recommendation for the mains could have been better.

Something unique about Flute in comparison to most other restaurants is that a 5% service fee is included and charged to the bill. This is interesting because tipping in India is optional as far as I am aware. This resulted in a modest increase in the bill of around ₹100 for the three dishes. However I would usually tip more but because the service fee was included it made little sense to top anything and felt somewhat redundant.

The service was nice as per my expectation but this practice is one which I have encountered in few restaurants and certainly is not a norm and so is something to be aware about.

The restaurant otherwise was good though but slightly priced on the premium side.

I thought some items were inappropriately priced. One small roti at ₹88 (excluding any taxes) seemed like a rip off because it averaged 3-4 rotis on just one dish so felt a bit unusual seeing ₹300 on a side dish of a basic small roti.

That said, the ambience was quite nice. The restaurant was air-conditioned, comfortable and relaxing, with an IPL match playing alongside mild instrumental music which made for a calm dining atmosphere.

Overall, good starters and ambience, but inconsistent mains and somewhat inflated pricing.

Mutton Rogan Josh also stood out with its rich spicy and aromatic flavour. The Chicken Biryani that followed was aromatic and satisfying.

Desserts were a highlight – the Butterscotch Ice Cream, Malai Kulfi, and the indulgent Pull Over Chocolate Cake were all top-notch, especially the chocolate cake, which was rich and gooey.

featured_reviews.name: Yogen Sachdev
featured_reviews.review_text:
I finally revisited Maaslli – Saraswat and GSB Speciality last night for my annual catch-up with friends, and once again, it reminded me why this place is rightly awarded the best seafood restaurant in Mumbai.

We started off with their seafood soup, which was practically a treasure hunt in a bowl, packed with so many varieties of seafood that I stopped trying to count after a few spoonfuls. A rich, flavorful start that set the tone for the evening.

Next came the Bombil Fry, and let me say this: if you visit Maaslli and skip this, you’re missing the highlight of the menu. Perfectly crisp on the outside, melt-in-your-mouth inside, it was unanimously the table favorite.

The Prawns Ghee Roast, their signature dish, followed, aromatic, buttery, and spicy in all the right ways. You could taste the freshness of the prawns through the layers of ghee and masala.

I ordered the cucumber mint cooler as a palette cleanser, one of the best non-alcoholic drinks I’ve had. Truly impressed by the bar at this outlet

To round things off, we indulged in the Crab Gravy with Bhakri, a true coastal comfort combination. The gravy had that home-style depth of flavor that only comes from slow cooking and authentic spices.

Between the impeccable flavors, warm service, and the nostalgic coastal touch in every dish, Maaslli continues to set the gold standard for seafood in Mumbai. Can’t wait for next year’s reunion, though honestly, I might not wait that long to go back.

Review: Soam Restaurant, Mumbai

We stay in Chembur and our family visited Soam restaurant in SoBo for the first time and enjoyed a truly satisfying vegetarian dining experience.

We ordered a wide spread of dishes — panki, sev puri, dahi puri, dahi bhalla chaat, watana ghughra, sada dosa, aloo puri with potato subji, thepla with red potato subji, moong dal khichadi and kadhi. Each item was flavorful, well‑prepared, and appreciated by everyone at the table.

The service was prompt and courteous, making the meal smooth and enjoyable. The atmosphere was decent, not extraordinary, but comfortable enough for a relaxed family outing.

One point worth noting is the pricing. Compared to similar restaurants in the suburbs, Soam is on the higher side. Perhaps this is the premium for being a very popular SoBo (South Bombay) restaurant.

Overall, Soam impressed us with its authentic flavors and variety. It’s a place we would recommend to anyone looking for wholesome vegetarian food in South Mumbai, while keeping in mind the pricing.

featured_reviews.name: 1TeaspoonLove
featured_reviews.review_text:
Sunday brunch at this Rooftop Cafe was a symphony of flavors, sounds, and warmth.

The anti-pasti spread was a visual feast, with a colorful array of dips, cheeses and salads. Each bite was a masterclass in textures and flavors, with the perfect balance of tangy, spicy, sweet and savory notes. Total hit. Must try.

The refreshing mocktails were the perfect accompaniment to the meal, with unique flavor combinations that tantalized my taste buds.

The mains however could have been better. The spaghetti aglio e olio was dry and little overcooked.
The nachos were delicious.
The potato Rosti was loaded with black pepper making it difficult to eat.

The desserts were good.

The live music added a delightful ambiance with the musician's soulful voice.

I would definitely recommend it to anyone looking for a leisurely and indulgent weekend treat.

featured_reviews.name: shripad marathe
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently discovered Cafe Calma, nestled in the iconic Shalimar Hotel, Kemps Corner, and I'm still reeling from the experience!

Ambience: 5/5
The rooftop setting offers breathtaking views of the city, making it perfect for a relaxing Sunday Brunch.

Food: 5/5
The unlimited antipasti spreads are a game-changer! With new themes every week, you'll get to indulge in a variety of flavors, from classic Mediterranean to modern European.

Service: 5/5
The staff is warm, attentive, and knowledgeable. They'll ensure you have a fantastic time!

Value for Money: 5/5
At ₹2000 per person, this Sunday Brunch experience is a steal!

Overall, Cafe Calma is a must-visit for anyone looking for a tranquil dining experience with great food, stunning views, and exceptional service.

Will I return? Absolutely!

featured_reviews.name: sachin moghe
featured_reviews.review_text:
last week happened to be in the area. had read numerous reviews about this restaurant as one of the best in girgaon hence dropped by for lunch.
location is excellent. near to charni road station (e). right on a traffic intersection. cannot miss.
place is very small and cramped. each table is meant to accomodate four but the seats are so small that only two can sit comfortably, one on either side. the restaurant was being attended by only one wait staff hence service as delayed.
i had ordered chicken sukka thali with tandoori roti. thali had two rotis, chi sukka, gravy, solkadhi and kanda nimbu. chicken was ordinary, large pieces about 4-5 but more of bone and very little meat. the masala was very spicy quite unlike manglori masala which is coconutty and flavourful. the gravy which came along with thali was ok. I was given another bowl of gravy alongwith rice. the waiter specifically asked me to have this gravy alongwith rice. this gravy was so spicy that my entire mouth was on fire. I had to leave half the rice uneaten. solkadhi was good. I wanted to order a glass but due to bad experience with other items in the thali, did not order solkadhi again.
there is nothing manglori about solkadhi hence don't understand why do manglori restaurants serve solkadhi. I won't be surprised if tomorrow these people say that solkadhi is originally a manglori dish.
hopeless place. the person sitting in front of me was having fish fry thali and the expression on his face clearly indicated that he too was disappointed.
bad place. could be ignored. there is nothing modern about this place. there are many better places than this one nearby. while walking from charni road metro to this place I passed by panshikar ahar which is truly iconic. after finishing my lunch or rather half eaten lunch i regretted my decision to enter this place.

We stumbled upon this hidden gem completely by chance while looking for a spot to celebrate our one-month anniversary, and it couldn't have been more perfect. If you are looking for a place that nails the balance between a romantic date-night vibe and an incredible culinary experience, this is it.

The moment we walked in, the atmosphere set the mood. It features a gorgeous, well-stocked bar and the absolute perfect playlist—romantic, soulful music that was acoustic and intimate, but just the right volume so we could actually talk and connect. It felt incredibly cozy and special.

Uppa (uppaddeen) was serving us snd he was very gentle in his talks snd suggested these delicious starters / small plates. We also ordered a pizza, I’m forgetting which one. We could barely eat 4 slices of this pizza and by then we were fully satiated. So we requested them to pack it for us.

Enjoyed very much and am looking forward visiting them again. VERY SOON. Although there are many many other cafés and restaurants that I must visit. So good bye for now.

Do dine here and you will enjoy.

featured_reviews.name: tushar alphonso
featured_reviews.review_text:
A Hidden Gem for Seafood Lovers!
Stepping into Restaurant was like discovering a true culinary treasure. This charming, intimate seafood restaurant, though small in size, delivers an experience from the moment you walk in, the ambiance wraps around you like a warm, welcoming net. It's cozy and tastefully decorated, creating the perfect setting for a relaxed and enjoyable meal. You can tell a lot of thought went into making the space feel both elegant and comfortable.

But let's talk about the star of the show: the seafood! Every dish we ordered was simply divine. The prawns koliwada, bombil fry, chicken lollipop, Surmai fry, PRAWNS biryani & Paneer Biryani, Potato Kappa was cooked to perfection, showcasing the incredible freshness of the ingredients. It's clear they pride themselves on sourcing good quality seafood. The flavors were vibrant, perfectly balanced, and truly unforgettable.

The service was also impeccable – attentive without being intrusive, and genuinely friendly.

If you're a seafood enthusiast looking for an extraordinary dining experience in a delightful setting, [Masta Gajali] is an absolute must-visit. It's a small place with a huge heart and even bigger flavors. Highly, highly recommended!

featured_reviews.review_text:
I had ordered their Bombil Thali and Prawn Samosa through Zomato from their Mazgaon branch. I was highly impressed with the packing and the good portions of the Bombil pieces. ​I truly believe one shouldn't speak ill of food, but I had an absolutely terrible experience here.
​We ordered the Prawns Koliwada and Crispy Chicken. Given the massive hype surrounding this restaurant, we expected the food to be exceptional. As a seafood lover—especially prawns fry—I was genuinely shocked from the very first bite. The Prawns Koliwada was completely tasteless; the spice profile was missing and there was no salt at all.
​To make matters worse, when my wife cut into a prawn, we realized they hadn't been cleaned properly. The digestive tracks (veins) were still inside. Every single prawn was like that, which completely ruined our appetite. On top of that, the dish was incredibly expensive.

​The Crispy Chicken
​The second dish was just as bad. It was so sour that after just one bite, we had to ask the waiter to pack it up. Neither my wife nor my kids could eat it—it was a total waste of money. I’ve had Crispy Chicken at many places, but this was the worst. Honestly, the local Chinese joint in my neighborhood makes it better.

​The Lesson Learned
​This experience taught me one thing: don't just rush to a restaurant based on an influencer's video. You have to check real reviews first. I have no idea what people actually like about the food there. My wife and I are beyond disappointed.

Ambiance: Simple, soothing, with both indoor and outdoor sitting. Located at Babhai Naka, Borivali.

Our experience: We went in for dinner on a weekday. The place was largely empty and quiet. Took them 20 mins to take our first order despite having only 4 tables being served including ours.

• Bangda Thali and Ravas thali: Both thalis were exactly the same with the same fish curry, a tiny serving of prawn preparation, another tiny serving of matki usal in one thali and another random gravy in the bangda thalis. We weren't asked about our preferences for wada, chapati or bhakri. So one thali came with wadas, the other with chapati and on placing the order the third, we were asked about our preference for chapati or bhakri then informed bhakri is probabaly over. So we okayed chapati but were served wadas.

We also ordered another plate of extra chapati which they didnt have and offered wadas but none reached our table even after 2 reminders.

Finally we finished our meals and then asked for the bill which had the extra cost of wadas which we ordered and never recieved and also for the wada in thali which we weren't informed were charged extra but were given as they didnt have chapatis or bhakris.

They did change the bill on being informed.

We also asked for regular water which we recieved almost at the end of the meal after being reminded for the fifth time.

Service: Slow, and confused even when there were just 2-3 tables with people only.

While we understand it was end if the day and hence the food there was over and also probably that is why there were many errors & delays in service. But the overall experience and food were not upto the mark or hype.

featured_reviews.name: Janhavi Raut
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited Goankar Cuisine in Mumbai, and overall it turned out to be a mixed but interesting dining experience. When we first arrived, the restaurant was completely empty, but as we started ordering, the place quickly became busy and was soon filled with many guests.

We began with crab Manchow soup, but honestly it tasted more like a regular Manchow soup as the crab quantity was very minimal and there wasn’t much seafood flavour in it. After that, we tried prawns lollipop, which unfortunately was not good. The texture felt sticky and unusual, and it was difficult to even recognize the prawns properly, so we didn’t enjoy that dish.

However, the experience improved with the next dishes. The squid Koliwada was excellent — very crunchy and perfectly cooked. It was definitely one of the better starters we tried.

The staff member Mr. Akash, who was serving us, was very helpful and gave good suggestions. On his recommendation, we tried chicken Kalakari, which turned out to be really tasty. It had a rich, authentic Indian-style chicken masala and was well marinated with great flavour.

For the main course, he first suggested chicken vindaloo, but since it is slightly tangy, we decided not to order it. Instead, he recommended chicken Xacuti (Shakoti), which was excellent and full of authentic Goan flavours. Along with that, we tried prawns masala dry, which was honestly amazing and one of the highlights of the meal.

We paired the dishes with Amboli, Ghavna, and rice bhakri. The rice bhakri was very large and quite filling, making it a great accompaniment to the curries.

For dessert, we tried Ukdiche Modak ice cream, which was truly a game changer. It was such a unique dessert that we ended up ordering another one because everyone at the table loved it. It was a really creative and delicious twist on the traditional modak.

Overall, despite a few disappointing starters, the main course, dessert, and the helpful service by Mr. Akash made the experience really enjoyable. If you visit, definitely try the squid Koliwada, prawns masala dry, chicken Xacuti, and the Ukdiche Modak ice cream.

featured_reviews.name: priyanka mustafi
featured_reviews.review_text:
Good food, quite authentic in taste. We had prawn manchow soup which was loaded with prawns. Their prawn lollypops are great, we also had squid tawa masala which was a bit salty but well cooked. We ordered thalis which was the main aim. Surmai and pomfret. The size was very good and fish was fresh. The thali was very good - rice, bhakri ( u can choose amboli or even chapati) , bhurji, sukka, prawn curry, bangda curry, salad and ofcourse rawa fry of the fish you choose. The place is very tiny with only 8 tables but service is prompt and nice ambience for a homely meal
.

featured_reviews.name: Vinayak Moorthy
featured_reviews.review_text:
Goaikar – where the fish is larger than life and the flavours come with a warning ⚠️🐟

Walked into Goaikar with big Goan expectations and walked out with an even bigger respect for their humongous fish portions. Let’s start with the clear winners of the day — the prawns lollipop and the stuffed bombil fry. Absolute show-stealers. Crisp, juicy, perfectly seasoned… the kind of dishes that make you nod silently while chewing because words fail you.

Next up, the iconic Goan ros omelette with poee — decent, comforting, but didn’t quite give us that nostalgic roadside Goan punch. More “okay okay” than “arre waah”.

Now to the grand thali saga 🍽️
We ordered the Surmai fish thali, Pomfret special thali, and Bombil thali — and oh my God, the fishes were MONSTERS. Fried to golden perfection, fresh, meaty, and clearly not shy about their presence on the plate. Total paisa-vasool when it comes to the fish itself.

But (there’s always a but)… the accompanying curries and gravies came in hot — and not the fun kind 🌶️🔥
For us, especially with a Goan mom in the house, the gravies felt too spicy and a little off-track from traditional Goan flavours. More fire, less finesse. Authentic Goa whispered… while chilli shouted.

Just when our taste buds were waving a white flag, dessert arrived like a saviour from heaven — Ukdiche Modak Ice Cream 🍨✨
Sweet, comforting, innovative, and honestly the icing on the cake (or modak on the ice cream?). A perfect, soulful ending that brought smiles back instantly.

From a value standpoint, pricing sits firmly at the premium end, with most dishes priced at ₹500 and above. While the generous seafood portions partially justify this, the ukdiche modak ice cream, though innovative and flavourful, was served in a modest portion at ₹180, feeling more like a tasting than a finale.

It is also worth noting that several social media claims suggesting a 10% discount at the restaurant did not reflect our experience, and no such concession was available during our visit—something diners may wish to verify in advance.

What truly elevated the experience was the service. Our order taker, Aditya, was exceptionally warm, attentive, and knowledgeable, guiding us with genuine enthusiasm. The entire service team mirrored this standard—courteous, efficient, and consistently welcoming—adding a layer of hospitality that made the meal feel relaxed and well cared for.

Final verdict:
Goaikar nails seafood portions and frying like a boss, experiments boldly with flavours, and redeems everything with dessert magic. A must-visit for fish lovers — just keep a glass of water (and an open mind for spice) handy 😄🔥🐠

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ (minus half a star for the chilli ambush)

featured_reviews.review_text: Looked good. Good quantity. Clean but not tasty. As a goan I know my cuisine and this isn't goan at all.  Curry had no taste. Fish fry was ok.

featured_reviews.name: Shraddha Nayak
featured_reviews.review_text: Food was good, we started with bombil and mandeli fry, then we ordered pompret thali in which the bangda curry was really yummy. Then we tried Chicken xacuti poees which was good too. The highlight was the dessert Ukadiche modak ice-cream. Overall amazing service and atmosphere.
